observations: Answered from the idle desktop screenshot before any source: purpose read as an account-settings page (cards titled 'Profile', 'Preferences', 'Projects', 'Danger zone' for user Alex Rivera) — matches the brief exactly.
Primary action read as the single filled teal 'Save changes' button; the source confirms it is the only .btn.primary on the idle page and metrics record primaryAction = BUTTON 'Save changes'.

Attention read as the 'Danger zone' card: red hazard-stripe top border, red header, three filled red risk bars labelled 'IRREVERSIBLE', outlined red 'Delete account' button — precisely the destructive surface the brief asks for; the amber 'Setup incomplete' chip is the correct secondary attention point.
Both deletion paths named in the brief are visible at a glance: per-row trash icon buttons on all 3 project rows and the 'Delete account' button, so nothing the brief requires is buried.
Raw ratio: 3/3 inventory items are graphical+text; 0 text only, 0 missing. Metrics back this: graphical.total = 34 on desktop (20 svg, 1 progress, 13 badges) against only 64 visible words.

Save state is graphical at every stage: the amber .dot-mod dirty dot on edited fields, a spinner replacing the save icon with label 'Saving' and aria-busy, a green check SVG + 'Saved' note, the header status pill switching among spinner/'Saving', check/'Saved', alert/'Action failed' (visible in the error screenshot), and toggle switches that show a mid-position knob with an embedded spinner while pending.

Destructive-action danger level is graphical: repeating red hazard-stripe .hatch bars on the danger card, the modal, the load-error card and the terminal screen; a three-segment .risk bar meter with 'IRREVERSIBLE'; warning-triangle SVGs; red outlined vs red filled button tiers ('Delete account' vs 'Delete forever'); red loss chips in the modal ('3 projects', 'Pro plan', 'No undo').

Confirmation state is graphical: an armed project row turns amber (data-armed background) with a warning icon and Keep/Delete split; the modal shows a lock icon whose SVG physically opens when the typed email matches, with text state 'Email must match' → 'Unlocked'; a red <progress> bar (#mBar) runs across the modal while deleteAccount is pending and on the deleting project row.
Desktop pageWords is 64 for the entire page — the UI shows state through icons, chips and color rather than prose; helperWords = 6 and longLeafWords = 0 with an empty longLeaves list.
All 5 button labels average 1.4 words with a max of 2 ('Save changes', 'Delete account', 'Delete forever', 'Cancel', 'Retry'); longLabels is empty.
The only helper sentence on the idle page, 'Removes your account and all projects.', adds information the heading does not carry (projects go too) rather than restating it.

Error copy is telegraphic and stateful, e.g. 'Profile not saved. Network error. Nothing changed.' — each fragment carries distinct information (what failed, why, resulting state); nothing narrates what the UI already shows.
Terminology is consistent end to end: 'Delete account' in the card, button, and modal title; 'project' everywhere; the Save/Saving/Saved triple reused identically for profile, preferences and theme.

Copy matches verified behavior: 'Delete forever' / 'No undo' precede a genuinely unguarded terminal state, and 'Account deleted. Confirmed by the server.' is literally true — the async rater confirmed success is only shown after the promise resolves (item 10 PASS).

Error messages are specific, not filler: '"Q3 Website Rebuild" not deleted. Network error. Nothing changed.' names the object, cause and resulting state; fallbacks ('Unnamed account', 'Unknown date', 'Not found on the server.') are all real strings, no lorem or TODO placeholders.
No marketing tone anywhere; the closest to voice is the empty-state line 'Nothing left to delete here.', which is accurate for this deletion-centric settings context rather than filler.

Multiple color and layout decisions exist only because this brief is about destruction: hazard-stripe .hatch borders reserved for destructive/failed surfaces, a three-bar 'IRREVERSIBLE' risk meter, a two-tier red button system (outlined 'Delete account' to open, filled 'Delete forever' to commit), and live loss chips ('3 projects', 'Pro plan', 'No undo') computed from the actual account.

The confirmation interaction is bespoke: inline arm/Keep/Delete on each project row (row turns amber) instead of a generic modal, and a type-your-email gate whose lock icon SVG visibly opens on match — not stock components.

The base visual language is the standard SaaS settings template: white cards on #eef0f3, Inter, teal accent, pill chips, iOS-style toggles, shimmer skeletons, two-column card grid — competent but interchangeable.

Small task-aware touches: JetBrains Mono for project ids/dates, the deleted-account terminal 'seal' screen replacing the entire shell, and the header status pill that aggregates any in-flight mutation.

f4TaskDriven: Hazard-stripe .hatch borders applied only to destructive and failure surfaces (danger card, delete modal, load-error card, terminal deleted screen)
Three-segment risk bar meter with uppercase 'IRREVERSIBLE' label above the delete-account row
Two-tier destructive buttons: outlined 'Delete account' to open the flow, filled red 'Delete forever' to commit
Modal loss chips enumerating the concrete stakes from live data: '3 projects', 'Pro plan', 'No undo'
Type-your-email confirmation gate with a lock icon that visually unlocks on match and states 'Email must match' / 'Unlocked'
Inline per-row arm/Keep/Delete confirmation that turns the project row amber instead of a generic dialog
Terminal 'Account deleted / Confirmed by the server.' seal screen that replaces the whole shell
Amber dirty-dots on modified profile fields tied to the save state
JetBrains Mono for project ids and dates in the projects list
Empty-state copy 'Nothing left to delete here.' acknowledging the page's deletion purpose
f4Template: White cards on light-grey (#eef0f3) background with subtle shadow — stock SaaS settings look
Inter as the UI typeface with a teal accent color, both interchangeable with any dashboard
iOS-style toggle switches and pill-shaped chips/badges
Shimmer skeleton loaders for header, inputs and project rows
Two-column card grid collapsing to one column on mobile — standard responsive settings layout
